title: (Why) Jets quantise trapped acoustic modes
summary: High-subsonic turbulent jets trap acoustic modes in their potential core. The modes lie in narrow frequency bands that are $O(0.1)$-wide in Strouhal number, $St$. By studying a Mach 0.9, Reynolds number $10^6$ jet, this work confirms an earlier hypothesis: each band is made up of $O(10)$ discrete frequencies, $ΔSt \sim O(0.01)$ apart. To resolve them, we collect $O(100\,000)$ snapshots from dedicated schlieren experiments and large-eddy simulations (LES), and apply spectral proper orthogonal decomposition (SPOD).
